Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Sunil Kumar Tiwari
Hon'ble Raj Beer Singh,J.
1. Heard learned counsel for the applicants, learned counsel for the opposite party no.2/informant
and learned A.G.A. for the State.
2.

This application u/s 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed with the prayer to quash the entire proceedings,
including charge-sheet dated 07.02.2024 as well as cognizance/summoning order dated 11.03.2024,
of Case No. 6314 of 2024 (State Vs. Raman Grewal and others), arising out of case crime no. 116 of 2023, under Sections - 498A, 323, 328, 506 IPC and Section - 3/4 D.P. Act, P.S.- Ramraj,, District- Muzaffarnagar, pending in the court of Civil Judge, S.D., F.T.C., Muzaffarnagar.

sentences.text: After arguing at some length, learned counsel counsel for applicants submits that applicants are not pressing the prayer of quashing of proceedings and instead of that applicants may be permitted to move an application for discharge before the trial court and till the disposal of discharge application some interim protection may be granted.

4. Learned A.G.A. and learned counsel for the informant have opposed the application and submitted that anticipatory bail application of applicant no.1 Raman Grewal is pending and that earlier in Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. 884 of 2024, applicant no.1 was directed to appear before the court concerned within a period of 60 days but he has not surrendered.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. 884 of 2024
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: 5. In view of aforesaid, it is directed that in case applicants move an application for discharge before the trial court concerned within a period of three weeks from today, the same shall be considered and decided expeditiously in accordance with law by the court concerned.

It is further directed that for a period of three weeks from today and in case such an application for discharge is filed within the aforesaid period, till the disposal of said discharge application, no coercive action shall be taken against the applicant no.2, 3 and 4, namely, Sukhdev Singh, Jasmel Kaur and Kirandeep Kaur,
provided the applicants cooperate in early disposal of discharge application.
6. The instant application u/s 482 Cr.P.C. is disposed of with aforesaid observations.
